title.narrative: Emergency WASH support to IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable Host Communities in Renk County, South Suda

description.narrative: Recent Needs Assessment conducted by CTP in Upper Nile State has found that predominantly open defecation is practices due to no access to latrines and few households that have access to latrines are not engaging in hand-washing after latrine use. The consequences of poor sanitation and hygiene leave children vulnerable to malnutrition and opportunistic infections like pneumonia. Communities situated along river banks, or near chronically flooded areas as Renk, rely on unsafe surface water for domestic purposes therefore exposing the community to dangers of diarrhoea and other water borne related diseases. Beyond infrastructural deficiencies, traditional beliefs, cultural practices and lack of information are seen as the highest contributing factors to poor hygiene behaviours in Renk. The main outcome of the project will be emergency latrine construction and hygiene promotion to Households affected by current armed conflict. The impact of the project will be that 700 households in the two Payams of Renk County that is, Renk and Geiger Payams of Upper Nile and 3 target schools (2000 girls and boys) will have access to sanitation facilitaties and be aware of hygiene and sanitation practices. The project will be implemented from during the dry season from Feb to April 2016. The project will work with school children, returnees, IDPs and host communities.
